records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ לֵ֣ךְ עֲלֵ֣ה מִזֶּ֔ה אַתָּ֣ה וְהָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱלִ֖יתָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֶל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִ֠שְׁבַּעְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֨ם לְיִצְחָ֤ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹב֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְזַרְעֲךָ֖ אֶתְּנֶֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, go, go up from here, you and the people whom you brought up from [the] land of Egypt, to the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, saying, to your offspring I will give it.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Move on from here, you and the people whom you led up out of the land of Egypt. Head for the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the land of which I said, 'To your offspring I will give it.'

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, "Go, go up from here, you and the people whom you have brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, 'To your offspring I will give it.'

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Leave this place. Take the people you brought out of Egypt and go to the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. I told them, 'I will give this land to your descendants.'

decisions.choice: you and the people whom you brought up: God speaks of Israel as Moses' people
decisions.reason: God uses the same words as in 32:7, "your people, whom you brought up". He does not here call them "my people" or say that he brought them up (contrast 3:10; 20:2). Moses answers this in verse 13: "this nation is your people".

decisions.choice: the land which I swore: the promise to the patriarchs still stands
decisions.reason: God swore the land to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Genesis 12:7; 26:3; 28:13; Exodus 6:8; 32:13). Even after the golden calf, the promise of the land is not withdrawn; what is in question is whether God himself will go with them (verse 3).

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: Readable says "descendants" for "offspring" (literally "seed"), the children born to the patriarchs' line.

records.heading: A grim message and the tent outside the camp

records.source: וְשָׁלַחְתִּ֥י לְפָנֶ֖יךָ מַלְאָ֑ךְ וְגֵֽרַשְׁתִּ֗י אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י וְהַֽחִתִּי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I will send before you an angel, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite and the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite.
pieces: I will send an angel ahead of you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

L.2: And I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.

R.2: I will send an angel to go ahead of you. I will force out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

decisions.choice: I will send an angel before you: the messenger promised in 23:20 and 32:34
decisions.reason: God had promised an angel to guard Israel on the way (23:20-23) and repeated it after the golden calf (32:34). Here the angel is offered in place of God's own going among them (verse 3), which is what Moses goes on to plead for (verses 12-16).

decisions.choice: the Canaanite ... the Jebusite: each name stands for a whole people
decisions.reason: Each name is singular with the article, a way of naming a whole people. The same list of peoples appears in 3:8, 17 and 23:23.

decisions.choice: Canaanites ... Jebusites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for each people; Literal keeps the singular.

records.source: אֶל־אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א אֶֽעֱלֶ֜ה בְּקִרְבְּךָ֗ כִּ֤י עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֨רֶף֙ אַ֔תָּה פֶּן־אֲכֶלְךָ֖ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃
records.gloss: To a land flowing [with] milk and honey; for not I will go up in your midst, for a people stiff of neck you [are], lest I make an end of you on the way.
pieces: Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up among you myself, since you are a stiff-necked people, and I might put an end to you on the road."

L.3: [Go up] to a land flowing [with] milk and honey; for I will not go up in your midst, for you [are] a stiff-necked people, lest I make an end of you on the way."

R.3: Go to that land so rich with milk and honey. But I will not go with you myself. You are a stubborn people, and I might destroy you on the way."

decisions.choice: a stiff-necked people: stubborn, refusing to be led
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox or other animal that stiffens its neck and will not bend to the yoke or the driver. God used the phrase of Israel just after the golden calf (32:9), and it returns in verse 5 and 34:9.

decisions.choice: I will not go up in your midst, lest I make an end of you: God's nearness is a danger to a rebellious people
decisions.reason: The holy God dwelling among a stubborn people would mean their destruction, as 32:10 had threatened. Holding back his presence is here an act of mercy, but it is also a loss, which is why the people mourn (verse 4) and Moses pleads (verses 15-16).

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: a rich, fertile land
decisions.reason: The phrase first described the land in 3:8. Milk from flocks and herds and honey (from bees, or syrup from fruit) stand for plenty.

decisions.choice: [Go up] / Go up / Go
decisions.reason: The verse continues God's command from verse 1, "go up ... to the land". The verb is supplied to restart the sentence after verse 2. Readable says "stubborn" for "stiff-necked".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע הָעָ֗ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הָרָ֛ע הַזֶּ֖ה וַיִּתְאַבָּ֑לוּ וְלֹא־שָׁ֛תוּ אִ֥ישׁ עֶדְי֖וֹ עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And heard the people the word the bad the this, and they mourned, and not put anyone his ornaments on himself.
pieces: The people heard this grim message and grieved; not one of them put on their ornaments.

L.4: And the people heard this bad word, and they mourned, and no one put his ornaments on himself.

R.4: When the people heard this bad news, they were very sad. None of them wore their jewelry.

decisions.choice: this bad word: grievous news
decisions.reason: "Bad" here means painful or distressing. The news is that God will not go among them (verses 2-3).

decisions.choice: they mourned and put on no ornaments: outward signs of grief
decisions.reason: Leaving off jewelry and fine clothing was a sign of mourning and humbling oneself (2 Samuel 14:2; Ezekiel 26:16). The ornaments may include the jewelry asked of the Egyptians (3:22; 11:2).

decisions.choice: jewelry
decisions.reason: Readable says "jewelry" for "ornaments", the rings, earrings and other finery the people wore.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֱמֹ֤ר אֶל־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אַתֶּ֣ם עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֔רֶף רֶ֧גַע אֶחָ֛ד אֶֽעֱלֶ֥ה בְקִרְבְּךָ֖ וְכִלִּיתִ֑יךָ וְעַתָּ֗ה הוֹרֵ֤ד עֶדְיְךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְאֵדְעָ֖ה מָ֥ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, say to [the] sons of Israel, you [are] a people stiff of neck; [in] one moment [if] I go up in your midst, I will make an end of you. And now, take down your ornaments from on yourself, so that I may know what I will do to you.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'You are a stiff-necked people. Were I to go up among you even for a moment, I would put an end to you. So take off your ornaments now, and then I will settle what I am going to do about you.'"

L.5: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Say to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, 'You [are] a stiff-necked people. [If for] one moment I go up in your midst, I will make an end of you. And now, take down your ornaments from on yourselves, that I may know what I will do to you.'"

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Say to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'You are a stubborn people. If I went with you even for a moment, I might destroy you. Now take off your jewelry. Then I will choose what I will do with you.'"

decisions.choice: said: possibly "had said", explaining verse 4
decisions.reason: Verse 4 says the people did not put on their ornaments; verse 5 gives God's command to take them off, and verse 6 says they did. The verb may simply continue the story, or it may look back to what God had already said (the reason the people left off their ornaments). The verb form allows either.

decisions.choice: that I may know what I will do to you: God's decision is still open
decisions.reason: God speaks as one who will weigh the people's response before deciding. The taking off of the ornaments is a sign of repentance, and what follows (verses 12-17) shows God answering Moses' plea.

decisions.choice: one moment I go up in your midst: if I went with you even for a moment
decisions.reason: The clause is a condition without "if": were God to go among them even briefly, his presence would destroy them (verse 3).

records.source: וַיִּֽתְנַצְּל֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־עֶדְיָ֖ם מֵהַ֥ר חוֹרֵֽב׃
records.gloss: And stripped themselves [the] sons of Israel [of] their ornaments from [the] mountain of Horeb.
pieces: So from Mount Horeb onward the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} went without their ornaments.

L.6: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb [onward].

R.6: So from the time they were at Mount Horeb, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} no longer wore their jewelry.

decisions.choice: from Mount Horeb: from Horeb onward
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means that from their time at Horeb on, the people no longer wore their ornaments. It may instead mean only that they took them off there, at the mountain.

decisions.choice: Horeb: the mountain of God, also called Sinai
decisions.reason: Horeb is the name used for the mountain of God in 3:1 and 17:6; elsewhere in Exodus it is Sinai (19:11).

decisions.choice: stripped themselves: took off completely
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the Israelites "plundering" the Egyptians of their silver and gold (3:22; 12:36). Now Israel strips itself.

records.source: וּמֹשֶׁה֩ יִקַּ֨ח אֶת־הָאֹ֜הֶל וְנָֽטָה־ל֣וֹ׀מִח֣וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֗ה הַרְחֵק֙ מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְקָ֥רָא ל֖וֹ אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְהָיָה֙ כָּל־מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה יֵצֵא֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִח֥וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And Moses would take the tent and pitch it outside of the camp, far from the camp, and he called it [the] tent of meeting. And it was [that] everyone seeking Yahweh would go out to [the] tent of meeting, which [was] outside of the camp.
pieces: Moses made a practice of taking the tent and setting it up outside the camp, well away from it. He named it the tent of meeting. Whoever wanted to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went out to the tent of meeting beyond the camp.

L.7: And Moses would take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting. And it was [that] everyone seeking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would go out to the tent of meeting, which [was] outside the camp.

R.7: Moses used to take a tent and set it up outside the camp, a good distance away. He called it the tent of meeting. Anyone who wanted to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help or guidance went out to the tent of meeting outside the camp.

decisions.choice: the tent, the tent of meeting: a tent outside the camp, not the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The tabernacle described in chapters 25-31 has not yet been made; it is built in chapters 35-39 and set up only in 40:17. This tent stands outside the camp, while the tabernacle would stand in the middle of it (25:8; Numbers 2:2). Here a priest serves no altar; Moses goes out to meet God and Joshua keeps watch (verse 11). Later the name "tent of meeting" is used for the tabernacle itself (40:2).

decisions.choice: would take ... would pitch ... would go out: what was done again and again
decisions.reason: The verbs describe a regular practice, not a single event. Verses 7-11 tell how things were done during this period.

decisions.choice: everyone seeking Yahweh: anyone who wanted to inquire of God
decisions.reason: To seek God here means to come to ask his will or his help, as people came to Moses "to inquire of God" (18:15).

decisions.choice: ask the LORD for help or guidance
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "seeking" the LORD meant here.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה כְּצֵ֤את מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־הָאֹ֔הֶל יָק֨וּמוּ֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם וְנִ֨צְּב֔וּ אִ֖ישׁ פֶּ֣תַח אָהֳל֑וֹ וְהִבִּ֨יטוּ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה עַד־בֹּא֖וֹ הָאֹֽהֱלָה׃
records.gloss: And it was, as went out Moses to the tent, they would rise, all the people, and stand, each [at the] entrance of his tent, and they would look after Moses until he went into the tent.
pieces: When Moses set out for the tent, the whole people got to their feet. They stood, everyone at the door of their own tent, and followed Moses with their eyes until he went in.

L.8: And it was, as Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand, each [at] the entrance of {{gender:their|his}} tent, and they would look after Moses until he went into the tent.

R.8: Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people stood up. Everyone stood at the door of their own tent and kept their eyes on Moses until he had entered.

decisions.choice: they would rise and stand at the entrance of their tents: a sign of respect
decisions.reason: The people stood as Moses went out to meet God. Each household stayed at its own tent, watching from a distance.

decisions.choice: they would look after Moses: they watched him go
decisions.reason: The verb means to look closely or gaze. They watched Moses all the way to the tent.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה כְּבֹ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ הָאֹ֔הֱלָה יֵרֵד֙ עַמּ֣וּד הֶֽעָנָ֔ן וְעָמַ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל וְדִבֶּ֖ר עִם־מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And it was, as went Moses to the tent, would come down [the] pillar of the cloud and stand [at the] entrance of the tent, and he would speak with Moses.
pieces: Each time Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud came down and took its place at the tent's entrance, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke with Moses.

L.9: And it was, as Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand [at] the entrance of the tent, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would speak with Moses.

R.9: When Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud came down and stayed at the door of the tent. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} talked with Moses.

decisions.choice: he would speak: the LORD spoke, from the cloud
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. Verse 11 makes it clear that the LORD is the one who speaks; the cloud is the sign of his presence (13:21-22; 19:9).

decisions.choice: the pillar of cloud: the sign that led Israel out of Egypt
decisions.reason: The same pillar went before Israel from Egypt (13:21-22; 14:19). Here it comes down to the tent's entrance when Moses enters. The same thing happens at the tabernacle later (Numbers 12:5; Deuteronomy 31:15).

decisions.choice: the LORD
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, as verse 11 does.

records.source: וְרָאָ֤ה כָל־הָעָם֙ אֶת־עַמּ֣וּד הֶֽעָנָ֔ן עֹמֵ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל וְקָ֤ם כָּל־הָעָם֙ וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוּ֔וּאִ֖ישׁ פֶּ֥תַח אָהֳלֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And saw all the people the pillar of the cloud standing [at the] entrance of the tent, and rose all the people and bowed down, each [at the] entrance of his tent.
pieces: Seeing the pillar of cloud at the tent's entrance, the whole people would stand up and then bow low, everyone at the door of their own tent.

L.10: And all the people would see the pillar of cloud standing [at] the entrance of the tent, and all the people would rise and bow down, each [at] the entrance of {{gender:their|his}} tent.

R.10: When the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the door of the tent, they all stood up. Then they bowed down to worship, each at the door of their own tent.

decisions.choice: bowed down: worshiped
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low to the ground, the posture of worship (4:31; 12:27). The people worship toward the sign of God's presence.

decisions.choice: would see ... would rise: again a repeated practice
decisions.reason: As in verses 7-9, the verbs describe what happened each time.

decisions.choice: to worship
decisions.reason: Readable says why they bowed.

records.source: וְדִבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ פָּנִ֣ים אֶל־פָּנִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְדַבֵּ֥ר אִ֖ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְשָׁב֙ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וּמְשָׁ֨רְת֜וֹ יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ בִּן־נוּן֙ נַ֔עַר לֹ֥א יָמִ֖ישׁ מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֹֽהֶל׃ס
records.gloss: And would speak Yahweh to Moses face to face, just as speaks a man to his companion. And he would return to the camp, but his servant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, not would depart from [the] midst of the tent.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} would speak with Moses face to face, the way {{gender:a person|a man}} talks with a friend. Moses then went back to the camp; but Joshua son of Nun, the young man who served him, stayed in the tent and did not leave it.

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} would speak to Moses face to face, as {{gender:a person|a man}} speaks to {{gender:their|his}} companion. And he would return to the camp, but his attendant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from the midst of the tent.

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} talked with Moses directly, face to face, as friends talk with each other. Then Moses went back to the camp. But Joshua son of Nun, Moses' young helper, stayed at the tent.

decisions.choice: face to face, as a man speaks to his friend: directly and openly
decisions.reason: The phrase describes direct, personal speech, with no go-between, dream or riddle (Numbers 12:8; Deuteronomy 34:10). It does not mean Moses saw God's own face, which verse 20 says no one may see and live. It speaks of closeness, not of a sight of God.

decisions.choice: servant ... a young man: Joshua, Moses' assistant
decisions.reason: The word for "servant" is used of a personal attendant (24:13). "Young man" describes his role as a younger helper more than his exact age.

decisions.choice: did not depart from the tent: Joshua kept watch there
decisions.reason: While Moses returned to the camp, Joshua stayed at the tent, perhaps guarding it.

decisions.choice: directly, face to face
decisions.reason: Readable adds "directly" to show what "face to face" means here.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה רְ֠אֵה אַתָּ֞ה אֹמֵ֤ר אֵלַי֙ הַ֚עַל אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א הֽוֹדַעְתַּ֔נִי אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־תִּשְׁלַ֖ח עִמִּ֑י וְאַתָּ֤ה אָמַ֨רְתָּ֙ יְדַעְתִּ֣יךָֽ בְשֵׁ֔ם וְגַם־מָצָ֥אתָ חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to Yahweh, see, you [are] saying to me, bring up the people the this, but you not have made me know whom you will send with me. And you have said, I know you by name, and also you have found favor in my eyes.
pieces: Moses said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "You tell me, 'Bring this people up,' yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have not made known to me who is to go with me. You have also said, 'I know you by name, and you have found favor in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight.'

L.12: And Moses said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "See, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] saying to me, 'Bring up this people,' but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have not let me know whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will send with me. Yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have said, 'I know you by name, and also you have found favor in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes.'

R.12: Moses said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "You keep telling me to lead these people. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have not told me whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will send with me. You have said, 'I know you by name, and I look on you with kindness.'

decisions.choice: I know you by name: I know you personally and have chosen you
decisions.reason: To know someone by name is to know them closely and single them out (compare Isaiah 43:1; 45:3). God repeats the words in verse 17.

decisions.choice: you have found favor in my eyes: I look on you with kindness
decisions.reason: The phrase means to be accepted and treated with kindness by someone (Genesis 6:8). Moses builds on it in verses 13, 16 and 17.

decisions.choice: whom you will send with me: the angel of verse 2 is not enough
decisions.reason: God had promised to send an angel (verse 2), but Moses wants to know who will go with them, since God had said he himself would not (verse 3).

decisions.choice: I look on you with kindness
decisions.reason: Readable explains "you have found favor in my eyes".

records.heading: Moses asks for God's presence

records.source: וְעַתָּ֡ה אִם־נָא֩ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֜ן בְּעֵינֶ֗יךָ הוֹדִעֵ֤נִי נָא֙ אֶת־דְּרָכֶ֔ךָ וְאֵדָ֣עֲךָ֔ לְמַ֥עַן אֶמְצָא־חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וּרְאֵ֕ה כִּ֥י עַמְּךָ֖ הַגּ֥וֹי הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And now, if please I have found favor in your eyes, make me know please your ways, that I may know you, so that I may find favor in your eyes; and consider that your people [is] the nation the this.
pieces: Now, if I really stand in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor, please show me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways. Then I will know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and I will go on finding favor with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. And keep in mind that this nation belongs to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people."

L.13: And now, if, please, I have found favor in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes, make known to me, please, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways, that I may know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, so that I may find favor in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes. And consider that this nation [is] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people."

R.13: If I really have {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor, show me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways. Then I will know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} better and keep on having {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor. Do not forget that these people belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: your ways: how God acts and what he intends
decisions.reason: Moses asks to understand God's ways, his purposes and how he deals with his people (Psalm 103:7: "He made known his ways to Moses"). Knowing them, Moses will know God himself.

decisions.choice: consider that this nation is your people: Moses gives the people back to God
decisions.reason: In verse 1 (and 32:7) God spoke of "the people whom you brought up". Moses answers that they are God's own people.

decisions.choice: that I may know you: know God personally
decisions.reason: The verb is the same as in "I know you by name" (verse 12). Moses wants to know God as God knows him.

records.source: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר פָּנַ֥י יֵלֵ֖כוּ וַהֲנִחֹ֥תִי לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And he said, my presence will go, and I will give rest to you.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "My own presence will go along, and I will bring you to rest."

L.14: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "My face will go, and I will give rest to you."

R.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "I myself will go with you, and I will give you rest."

decisions.choice: my face: my presence, God himself
decisions.reason: "Face" here means God's own presence, God going in person rather than through an angel (verses 2-3; Deuteronomy 4:37; Isaiah 63:9).

decisions.choice: my presence will go: a promise, possibly a question
alternatives: Must my presence go with you?
decisions.reason: The words read most simply as a promise. Because the Hebrew has no question marker, some take them as a question ("Must my presence go?"), but Moses' reply in verse 15 and God's answer in verse 17 fit a promise better.

decisions.choice: I will give rest to you: settle you safely in the land
decisions.reason: "Rest" is security in the land after the journey, free from enemies (Deuteronomy 3:20; 12:9-10; Joshua 1:13). "You" is singular, addressed to Moses as the people's leader.

decisions.choice: The LORD answered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker. Readable says "I myself will go" for "my presence will go".

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑יו אִם־אֵ֤ין פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ הֹלְכִ֔ים אַֽל־תַּעֲלֵ֖נוּ מִזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to him, if not your presence [is] going, not bring us up from here.
pieces: Moses said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Unless {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence goes with us, do not make us leave this place.

L.15: And he said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face is not going, do not bring us up from here.

R.15: Moses said, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not go with us {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}, do not send us away from here.

decisions.choice: if your presence does not go: Moses would rather stay than go without God
decisions.reason: For Moses, the land without God's presence is not worth having. He takes up God's own word "face" from verse 14.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he said to him"; Balanced and Readable name Moses.

records.source: וּבַמֶּ֣ה׀יִוָּדַ֣ע אֵפ֗וֹא כִּֽי־מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲנִ֣י וְעַמֶּ֔ךָ הֲל֖וֹא בְּלֶכְתְּךָ֣ עִמָּ֑נוּ וְנִפְלֵ֨ינוּ֙אֲנִ֣י וְעַמְּךָ֔ מִכָּ֨ל־הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And by what will it be known then that I have found favor in your eyes, I and your people? [Is it] not in your going with us, and we are distinguished, I and your people, from every the people which [is] on [the] face of the ground?
pieces: How else will anyone know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look with favor on me and on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people? Is it not by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} going with us? That is what sets me and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people apart from every other people on the face of the earth."

L.16: And how then will it be known that I have found favor in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes, I and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people? [Is it] not in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} going with us, so that we are distinguished, I and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, from every people that [is] on the face of the ground?"

R.16: If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not go with us, how will anyone know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} accept me and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people? Your going with us is what makes us different from every other people on earth."

decisions.choice: we are distinguished: set apart, made distinct
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used when God set Goshen and Israel's livestock apart from Egypt (8:18; 9:4; 11:7). What marks Israel out from all peoples is that God goes with them.

decisions.choice: is it not in your going with us: the answer to Moses' own question
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "yes": only God's going with them will show his favor.

decisions.choice: sets ... apart / makes us different; the earth
decisions.reason: Balanced says "sets ... apart", as in 8:18, 9:4 and 11:7; Readable "makes us different". Both say "earth" for "ground".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה גַּ֣ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֑ה כִּֽי־מָצָ֤אתָ חֵן֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י וָאֵדָעֲךָ֖ בְּשֵֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, also the thing the this which you have spoken I will do, for you have found favor in my eyes and I have known you by name.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "This request too, the one you have just made, I will grant, because you have found favor in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight and I know you by name."

L.17: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Also this thing which you have spoken I will do, for you have found favor in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes, and I have known you by name."

R.17: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Moses, "Yes, I will do this too, just as you asked. You have {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} favor, and I know you by name."

decisions.choice: this thing too I will do: God grants Moses' plea
decisions.reason: God agrees to go with the people himself, as Moses asked (verses 15-16). He grants it for Moses' sake, because Moses has found favor.

decisions.choice: found favor ... known you by name: God repeats Moses' words from verse 12
decisions.reason: Moses quoted these words back to God (verse 12); now God affirms them.

records.heading: Moses asks to see God's glory

records.source: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַרְאֵ֥נִי נָ֖א אֶת־כְּבֹדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And he said, show me please your glory.
pieces: Then Moses said, "Please, let me see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory."

L.18: And he said, "Show me, please, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory."

R.18: Then Moses said, "Please let me see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} glory."

decisions.choice: your glory: God's own majesty, made visible
decisions.reason: God's glory had appeared in the cloud (16:10) and as fire on the mountain (24:16-17). Moses now asks to see God himself as fully as can be seen. God answers in verses 19-23.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he said"; Balanced and Readable name Moses.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֲנִ֨י אַעֲבִ֤יר כָּל־טוּבִי֙ עַל־פָּנֶ֔יךָ וְקָרָ֧אתִֽי בְשֵׁ֛ם יְהוָ֖ה לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְחַנֹּתִי֙ אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָחֹ֔ן וְרִחַמְתִּ֖י אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲרַחֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And he said, I will cause to pass by all my goodness before your face, and I will proclaim by [the] name Yahweh before you; and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "I will make all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} goodness go past you, and I will announce the name '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}' before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show compassion to whom I will show compassion."

L.19: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I will make all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} goodness pass before your face, and I will proclaim the name '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}' before you. And I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion."

R.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "I will make all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} goodness pass in front of you. I will call out the name '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}' so you can hear it. I will be kind to anyone I choose to be kind to. I will show mercy to anyone I choose to show mercy to."

decisions.choice: I will proclaim the name Yahweh: fulfilled in 34:5-7
decisions.reason: God does this when he passes before Moses and calls out his name and character: compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, full of steadfast love (34:5-7). What Moses sees is God's goodness and what he hears is God's name; the name tells who God is (3:14-15).

decisions.choice: I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious: God's mercy is his own free gift
decisions.reason: The form repeats the verb, like "I will be who I will be" in 3:14. God's grace and compassion are not earned or forced; he gives them freely, as he chooses. Paul quotes this verse in Romans 9:15.

decisions.choice: my goodness: God's kindness and good character
decisions.reason: Instead of his "glory" (verse 18), God speaks of his "goodness", the kindness spelled out in 34:6-7.

decisions.choice: be kind to anyone I choose ... show mercy to anyone I choose
decisions.reason: Readable puts the repeated form plainly as God's free choice.

records.source: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹ֥א תוּכַ֖ל לִרְאֹ֣ת אֶת־פָּנָ֑י כִּ֛י לֹֽא־יִרְאַ֥נִי הָאָדָ֖ם וָחָֽי׃
records.gloss: And he said, not you will be able to see my face, for not will see me man and live.
pieces: He went on, "My face you cannot see. No human being can see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and stay alive."

L.20: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "You are not able to see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face, for no human will see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and live."

R.20: He also said, "You are not able to look at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face. Anyone who sees {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will die."

decisions.choice: you cannot see my face: no one can bear the full sight of God
decisions.reason: "Face" is language drawn from human life, used of God to speak of his full presence. No human being can see him as he is and live (Genesis 32:31; Judges 13:22; John 1:18). This is set beside 24:10-11, where the elders "saw the God of Israel" yet only what lay under his feet is described, and verse 11, where "face to face" means direct speech.

decisions.choice: man: a human being
decisions.reason: The word means any human being, not a male.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֥ה מָק֖וֹם אִתִּ֑י וְנִצַּבְתָּ֖ עַל־הַצּֽוּר׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh, look, a place [is] with me, and you will stand on the rock.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "There is a place beside {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You are to stand there on the rock.

L.21: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Look, [there is] a place with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you will stand on the rock.

R.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Here is a place next to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You can stand on this rock.

decisions.choice: a place with me: a spot near God, on the mountain
decisions.reason: The place is on Mount Sinai, where Moses will stand the next morning (34:2).

decisions.choice: the rock: the rock of the mountain
decisions.reason: The article points to a particular rock on the mountain, where God will shelter Moses (verse 22).

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ בַּעֲבֹ֣ר כְּבֹדִ֔י וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךָ בְּנִקְרַ֣ת הַצּ֑וּר וְשַׂכֹּתִ֥י כַפִּ֛י עָלֶ֖יךָ עַד־עָבְרִֽי׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when passes by my glory, I will put you in [the] cleft of the rock, and I will cover my palm over you until I have passed by.
pieces: While {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory is going by, I will tuck you into a cleft of the rock and shelter you with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand until I have gone past.

L.22: And it will be, when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory passes by, I will put you in the cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} palm until I have passed by.

R.22: When {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory goes past, I will put you in a crack in the rock. I will keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand over you until I am past.

decisions.choice: the cleft of the rock: a crack or hollow in the rock face
decisions.reason: The word means a split or crevice, deep enough to hide in (Isaiah 2:21).

decisions.choice: I will cover you with my palm: God shields Moses from his own glory
decisions.reason: The palm or hand is language drawn from human life. It pictures God protecting Moses, so that seeing God's glory does not destroy him (verse 20).

decisions.choice: hand
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "hand" for "palm".

records.source: וַהֲסִרֹתִי֙ אֶת־כַּפִּ֔י וְרָאִ֖יתָ אֶת־אֲחֹרָ֑י וּפָנַ֖י לֹ֥א יֵרָאֽוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And I will remove my palm, and you will see my back, but my face not will be seen.
pieces: When I draw back {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, you will see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} back. But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face will not be seen."

L.23: And I will take away {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} palm, and you will see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} back, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face will not be seen."

R.23: Then I will take {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand away, and you will see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} back. But no one may see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face."

decisions.choice: my back ... my face: language drawn from the human body, used of God
decisions.reason: Back and face, like hand (verse 22), speak of God in human terms. Moses will see God only after he has passed by, the trace of his glory and not its full sight. The same chapter says God spoke with Moses "face to face" (verse 11), and 24:10 that the elders "saw the God of Israel"; those passages speak of direct meeting, this one of the limit on what a human being may see.

decisions.choice: my back: what is behind, or what comes after
decisions.reason: The word means the hinder parts or back side; it can also mean what follows after. Moses sees God from behind, as he passes.
